title: Soft burst throttler and early KV-preserve patch for graceful regional handoff
author: Diego Chen
description:
Motivation: In production we observed short-duration traffic bursts from a handful of tenants that cause transient SLO violations and aggressive early evacuation of nodes, which leads to KV cache loss and longer downstream latency during cross-region failover. This PR introduces a soft burst throttler that applies a short, token-bucket based dampening window per-tenant and a coordinated 'early-kv-preserve' flag for evacuation to avoid discarding warm KV caches during fast handoffs.

What this change does: Adds an adaptive soft-burst-throttler component in the request admission path that: (1) detects sub-second CPU/queue spikes per-tenant and applies a light-rate cap that decays over 10-30s, (2) prefers gentle shedding (HTTP 429 with Retry-After) for best-effort tenants while keeping latency SLO tenants routed, and (3) emits telemetry to allow fast tuning. The early-kv-preserve patch extends the evacuation protocol: when a node receives an evacuation signal it marks selected KV shards with preserve=true and exposes a short-lived bridgelet token that target nodes can use to pull warmed KV segments instead of forcing a full recompute. This reduces cold-start penalties during regional failover.

Implementation notes: The throttler is implemented in runtime/admission/soft_burst_throttler.go and wired into the admission chain with a low-overhead fast-path. Token bucket parameters are workload-tunable via admission.policy JSON with sane defaults (burst_capacity=10, refill_ms=200, decay_window_s=20). The early-kv-preserve flow introduces a control-plane handshake: runtime/kv/preserve.go and a small router change in routing/failover_bridgelet.go. To avoid control plane churn I added a rate limiter for preserve handshakes and a safety TTL for bridgelet tokens.

Testing and validation: Unit tests cover token accounting and decay behavior. Integration e2e tests simulate a 5x burst for 60s across 200 concurrent tenants and assert 99th percentile latency stays under configured SLO for priority tenants and that 95% of preserved-KV handoffs rehydrate with <15ms additional latency vs baseline. Load tests were run in perf-lab with the new admission policy toggled on and off. CI: build, unit, integration, and perf smoke all passed after two reruns when a flaky eviction test was stabilized.

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind admission.features.soft_burst_throttle (off by default). We will enable for a small cohort of customers behind a runtime flag for 48 hours and monitor latency SLOs and preserved-KV hit ratio. If metrics look good, we will progressively enable across regions over a week. Rollback path: toggle the feature gate off and trigger an immediate revocation of active bridgelets (telemetry captured).

Checklist:
- [x] Add soft burst throttler runtime component
- [x] Add early-kv-preserve control handshake and bridgelet token flow
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Perf lab validation and dashboards
- [x] Docs snippet in ops/README about new admission policy

Related work: Builds on ideas from ENG-3721 (adaptive admission) and SRE-98 (regional failover telemetry). This is a targeted hotfix to reduce incident recurrence tied to rapid eviction loops observed during the October regional spike.

Notes on safety and observability: New metrics: admission.soft_burst.throttle_rate, admission.soft_burst.throttled_tenants, kv.preserve.handshakes, kv.preserve.success_rate, kv.preserve.latency_ms. Alerts: add a short-term guard if throttle_rate stays >50rps for >5m or preserve_success_rate <90% after rollout.

Files changed and rationale (high level): Keep diffs small and reviewable. The logic changes are scoped to the admission and kv modules and a tiny router tweak to consume bridgelet tokens. Low-risk to other components.
